title: Reject a horizon-independent retention bound from positive local coefficients
statement: A uniform hidden bit is encoded in the parity of T labels with terminal Bernoulli(lambda) noise. All ideal next-label probabilities remain in[lambda,1-lambda], while independent BSC(delta) outputs have only parity bias(1-2lambda)(1-2delta)^T. Their hidden-bit information decays exponentially although the one-use balanced coefficient is positive and parity costs O(T). This refutes naive sequential promotion, not the one-use theorem.
